We give more weight to stocks with higher forecast alpha relative to their residual variance. Kroger has the largest weight because its residual risk is relatively low.

How we calculate the weights

bᵢ = max(αᵢ, 0) / σ²(εᵢ)

xᵢ = bᵢ / Σbⱼ   ·   wᵢ = xᵢ / 3

x is a stock's share of the stock basket; w is its share of total NAV. Negative alpha gives zero weight. Risk comes from 60 monthly excess returns regressed on the SAA.

The common 50% haircut to valuation-based alpha is an assumption. Annual alpha estimates have considerable uncertainty over the short challenge horizon.

Why fund it this way?

Keep the SAA as the reference

Each ETF target becomes two-thirds of its original weight. This preserves the relative ETF mix while releasing capital for stocks.

Reduce the commodity position

DBC falls from 26.95% to 17.97% of NAV. It remains substantial, and Exxon adds further exposure to energy prices.

Use the portfolio's current value

The stock budget is $32,371,689.53, based on NAV of $97,115,068.58 after losses and distributions.

ADBEAdobe · 4.65% of NAV

$18.145 EPS × 16 = $290.32

Subscription cash flow supports the valuation. Our 16× GAAP earnings multiple allows for uncertainty over AI competition and renewals.

Catalyst. 9 December: results and the first FY2027 outlook. We will watch renewals and paid AI revenue.

Cash-flow check and main risk

FCFF value: $271.14. Lower of earnings and FCFF: $271.14. A 20% cut to normalized cash lowers the cash valuation to $216.54, below the $239.30 entry price.

KRKroger · 8.10% of NAV

$5.20 EPS × 15 = $78.00

Grocery demand and cash generation support a 15× adjusted earnings multiple. Low residual risk gives Kroger the largest stock weight.

Catalyst. 3 December: results should show whether the fulfillment reset supports sales and margins.

Cash-flow check and main risk

FCFF value: $87.45. Lower of earnings and FCFF: $78.00. Buybacks exceed cash available without new debt. Thin margins and leverage limit the case.

HRLHormel Foods · 6.90% of NAV

$1.48 EPS × 17 = $25.16

The 17× adjusted earnings multiple assumes recovering margins. This is a premium to our food peers and needs support from results.

Catalyst. 3 December: the first FY2027 outlook under the new CEO, with dividend coverage and Retail volumes in focus.

Cash-flow check and main risk

FCFF value: $31.49. Lower of earnings and FCFF: $25.16. Acquisition debt tightens dividend coverage. Full refinancing in our funding stress leaves coverage close to one.

BMYBristol Myers Squibb · 6.33% of NAV

$6.45 EPS × 11 = $70.95

An 11× guided earnings multiple allows for the patent cliff. The flat-cash valuation gives a smaller cushion at $65.50.

Catalyst. Pipeline readouts expected by year-end and ASH data on 12–15 December could improve confidence in replacement medicines.

Cash-flow check and main risk

FCFF value: $65.50. Lower of earnings and FCFF: $65.50. Trial outcomes are uncertain. The undated readouts could fall after 27 December, and declining cash flow erodes the valuation quickly.

XOMExxonMobil · 3.62% of NAV

$10.00 EPS × 18 = $180.00

Our $10 cycle-normalized EPS and 18× multiple depend on durable earnings from low-cost production. The smaller weight limits additional energy exposure.

Catalyst. Uaru start-up and the 2027 corporate plan are expected in Q4; both dates remain uncertain.

Cash-flow check and main risk

FCFF value: $213.08. Lower of earnings and FCFF: $180.00. This is our weakest catalyst on timing. A lower-cycle cash case gives $166.61, close to the $165.87 entry, and DBC already carries energy exposure.

HPQHP · 3.73% of NAV

$2.38 EPS × 13.5 = $32.13

We remove the $0.19 tariff-refund benefit from guided GAAP EPS, giving normalized EPS of $2.38. At 13.5×, the earnings value is $32.13.

Catalyst. 24 November: results and FY2027 guidance will test cash generation, memory costs and printing demand.

Cash-flow check and main risk

FCFF value: $34.44. Lower of earnings and FCFF: $32.13. Declining printing demand and PC costs can offset growth. Negative book equity makes cash coverage particularly important.

Cash-flow assumptions and stress tests

We forecast five years of FCFF and a terminal perpetuity, deduct stock-based compensation as an economic cost, and account for debt, cash and minority interests. Financing-consistent FCFE is a separate calculation check. The Excel model contains growth, rate, funding and price-convergence scenarios.

Holding weights fixed, forecast residual Information Ratio falls from 0.696 to 0.564 under the lower-value cash checks, and to 0.426 if every original fair value falls by 5%. For Adobe, cash-based annual IRR is 28.17% with full convergence after one year, 17.21% after three years, and 12.43% over three years if the initial discount persists.

What could change the market’s view?

The dates help us judge whether a valuation discount has a chance to close during the challenge.

  1. 24 November

    HP: results and FY2027 guidance

    Cash generation, PC margins and printing demand. Confirmed by the issuer.

  2. 28–29 November

    Next scheduled portfolio rebalance

    Several catalysts fall after this review. The annual alpha estimates extend beyond our current holding period.

  3. 3 December

    Kroger and Hormel: earnings and outlooks

    About 15% of NAV faces company news on the same day. We will watch Kroger's execution and Hormel's recovery and dividend coverage.

  4. 9 December

    Adobe: results and FY2027 outlook

    Renewals, pricing and paid AI demand will test the subscription cash-flow case.

  5. 12–15 December

    Bristol Myers Squibb: ASH data

    A dated opportunity for pipeline evidence. Other year-end trial readouts have uncertain timing.

  6. 27 December

    Challenge ends

    Exxon's Uaru and corporate-plan news, and BMY's undated readouts, could slip beyond this cutoff.

A scheduled report creates an opportunity for new information. Positive surprises and price convergence remain uncertain. Exxon's undated events give it the weakest timing case.

VaR assumes normal returns and zero mean: 1.645 × annual volatility / √12. Losses can exceed it. The original 8% volatility target applies to the SAA.

What we accepted

The monthly estimate fits the prescribed budget. Daily TE estimates of 6.53–7.74% and the historical validation below show substantial uncertainty around near-term risk. Kroger's 8.10% target also slightly exceeds our additional 8% single-stock preference. Both limitations are explicit in the report.

Testing different starting dates

We replay the fixed allocation over 33-session holding periods and compare its returns with the unchanged SAA. DBC changed its methodology on 10 November 2025, so we examine the earlier and later periods separately.

Historical active return

After the methodology change: 2025-11-10 to 2026-11-06. Zero trading fees.

Mean return above / below SAA-0.395%
Periods outperforming SAA44.2%
Overlapping holding periods217

The 217 overlapping periods contain only 6–7 non-overlapping windows per starting offset. The interval includes zero, and the later-period mean is below the SAA.

How to interpret these tests

We use today's selected stocks and assumptions throughout the history. Selection bias and repeated use of these data limit what the replay says about future returns. The many overlapping windows share observations. A block bootstrap allows for dependence when estimating the interval for mean active return.

At ten monthly historical forecast dates where monthly TE was within budget, realized 33-session daily TE subsequently exceeded 5% in 80% of cases. These dates also overlap. This result reinforces the uncertainty shown by our current daily risk estimates.

Read the test methodology and comparisons in the notebook ↗

How the forecast IR fits in

The stock basket has forecast residual IR of 0.696, including residual correlations. The classroom independence approximation gives 0.756. These estimates depend on our valuations and alpha haircut. The historical replay provides weak support for near-term outperformance, so we treat the forecast IR cautiously.

From research to the recorded allocation

The report and notebooks document the assumptions and calculations behind this page. Stock weights and quantities remain unchanged throughout the later valuation checks.

  1. Value the companies

    Choose normalized EPS and a P/E multiple, then examine financial quality, capital allocation, cash flow and catalyst timing.

  2. Translate the cases into alpha inputs

    Apply a common 50% haircut to annual full-convergence valuation premia. This is a judgment about uncertainty; the short challenge horizon calls for caution.

  3. Size and fund the basket

    Use alpha divided by residual variance, allocate one-third of NAV to stocks and scale the ETF targets proportionally. Compare all 420 three-to-six-stock combinations from nine researched names.

  4. Check the allocation and enter whole shares

    Test monthly and daily risk, staggered holding periods, cash assumptions and slower convergence. Use reconciled post-loss NAV and zero fees for the implementation quantities.
